Each tuple contains eight elements: probe name, target planet, current mass, engine thrust, solar drag, approach velocity, orbital pitch, and axial yaw. The system must model each probe using a dedicated class that stores these eight distinct attributes. The processing must be divided into three separate helper functions: one for assessing trajectory deviation, one for computing fuel expenditure, and one for generating an orbital insertion command. Each of these three helper functions must be defined to accept all eight attributes as individual distinct arguments, rather than accepting the object itself. The trajectory deviation evaluates current mass, engine thrust, and solar drag. The fuel expenditure adds approach velocity, orbital pitch, and axial yaw. The insertion command is a sentence detailing the probe name, target planet, and the two flight metrics. The main function will parse each tuple, instantiate the class, and pass the attributes from the class object to the three helper functions. Return a list of tuples containing the two numeric metrics and the insertion command sentence for each probe. For example, given a list with one tuple containing two strings and six numbers, it returns a list containing a tuple of two numbers and one sentence.

title: Document Page Typography Engine
spec: Write a text layout system starting with the entry function `typeset(paragraphs)`. The engine must format text by generating block layout tuples. A block is defined by its horizontal position float, vertical position float, width float, height float, typeface string, font size integer, tracking float, and alignment string. If the input is empty, return a default title page template containing exactly eight distinct layout blocks: a main title, a subtitle, an author name, a publisher imprint, a publication year, an international standard book number, a copyright notice, and a dedication. Each of these eight elements must be instantiated with specific, varying positioning and typography settings. For normal inputs, parse the text and map it to layout tuples based on the content. Example: empty input returns a list of eight tuples representing the title page layout.

title: Spirits Distillation Process Router
spec: Create a chemical configuration router with the entry function `distill(batches)`. The system configures the distillation column for different spirits. A configuration consists of tray count integer, boiler temperature float, column pressure float, reflux ratio float, feed rate float, solvent string, catalyst boolean, and heating ramp rate float. The logic must evaluate each batch string and return a configuration tuple. You must explicitly handle eight specific batch types: vodka, gin, light rum, dark rum, bourbon, rye whiskey, scotch, and tequila. Each type requires a unique combination of the eight configuration parameters to be generated and returned. Unknown types return a standard water purification configuration. Example: inputting a list with vodka and gin returns a list of two eight-element tuples.

title: Theme Park Animatronic Sequencer
spec: Develop a robotic motion controller using the entry function `sequence(actions)`. The controller translates action names into precise mechanical movement commands. A movement command is defined by the target joint string, target angle float, maximum velocity float, acceleration curve string, hold duration float, easing function string, start delay float, and execution priority string. The system must recognize and translate eight distinct predefined actions: wave, nod, point, bow, laugh, startle, idle, and deactivate. Each of these eight actions must map to a specific movement command with unique values for all eight mechanical parameters. If an action is unknown, return a safe shutdown command. Example: a sequence of wave and nod returns a list containing their respective eight element command tuples.

spec: Build a biological design tool starting with the entry function `assemble(genes)`. The tool designs genetic constructs by mapping gene identifiers to sequence assembly instructions. An instruction tuple contains the promoter sequence string, ribosome binding site string, coding region string, transcription terminator string, plasmid backbone string, selectable marker string, replication origin copy number integer, and read orientation string. The assembler must contain hardcoded blueprint definitions for eight specific common genes: insulin, glowing protein, growth hormone, antibiotic resistance, nitrogen fixation, pest resistance, drought tolerance, and flavor enhancement. Each must generate an instruction with distinct values for all eight biological parameters. Example: requesting insulin returns its corresponding eight element blueprint tuple.

title: Coastal Lighthouse Signal Designer

Each scenario requires the creation of a configuration tuple with eight specific settings. Example: processing a safe harbor station returns a tuple with its specific optical properties.

spec: Create an outdoor pursuit planner using the entry function `hide(waypoints)`. The planner maps adventure stages to physical and logical hide attributes. title: Bonsai Tree Aesthetics Evaluator
spec: Function `evaluate(trees)` processes miniature plant arrangements. Each tree is a tuple specifying trunk taper, branch placement, foliage density, root spread, pot harmony, age appearance, and overall balance. A tree is valid if taper is positive and foliage density exceeds root spread. For valid trees, calculate a score by multiplying age appearance by pot harmony, then adding trunk taper, branch placement, foliage density, root spread, and overall balance. title: Ceramic Glaze Formulation Calibrator
spec: Function `formulate(glazes)` processes batches of ceramic coatings. Discard batches where silica content is less than double the alumina ratio. For the remaining batches, determine the structural integrity by adding silica content, alumina ratio, flux modifiers, and colorant concentration, multiplying by firing temperature, and dividing the result by cooling rate. Finally, subtract the oxidation state. Return a list of final integrity values. Example input: a list containing one tuple with values ten, four, two, three, one thousand, fifty, and one. Expected output: a list containing one value of three hundred seventy nine.

A manuscript is restorable if vellum quality plus script legibility exceeds condition degradation. For restorable texts, compute a heritage value by adding gold leaf thickness, pigment rarity, margin width, and flourish complexity, multiplying the sum by vellum quality, and subtracting condition degradation. Return a list of heritage values, returning zero for unrestorable texts. Example input: a list containing one tuple with values two, five, eight, three, seven, four, and ten. Expected output: a list containing one value of one hundred two.

Expected output: a list containing one value of one hundred sixty six.

For passing designs, compute a comfort rating by adding lumbar support depth, seat pan tilt, armrest pivot angle, and headrest elevation, multiplying the sum by mesh tension, and subtracting caster friction. Return a list of growth multipliers, using zero for unviable ones. Example input: a list containing one tuple with values seventy, thirty, twenty five, two, forty, ten, and one hundred. Return a list of indices, using zero for invalid rooms. Example input: a list containing one tuple with values twenty, fifteen, ten, three, eight, five, and two. Expected output: a list containing one value of one hundred sixty nine.

For valid bags, calculate an insulation rating by adding down fill power, outer shell denier, hood cinch circumference, and lining reflectivity, multiplying by baffle height, and adding zipper draft thickness. Return a list of insulation ratings. Example input: a list containing one tuple with values eight hundred, four, twenty, three, thirty, fifty, and ten. spec: Must route books into rare, oversized, heavy, and fragile collections by executing `allocate(books)`. This requires validating the physical height, physical width, cover depth, total weight, publication year, rarity score, and binding material of each book against the shelf capacity, vertical clearance, humidity tolerance, and security level of the target zone. The logic must evaluate these seven book properties through separate placement formulas for the historical, reference, and display sections. Provide a summary of accepted and rejected books. Example input: a list containing a book with ten inches height, five inches width, two pounds, year eighteen fifty, score nine, leather binding. Output: a tuple of the accepted list and the rejected list.

title: Retail Mall Kiosk Allocator
spec: Assigns vendor booths to commercial mall zones using `configure(kiosks)`. The decision requires the kiosk width, depth, electrical power needs, water supply needs, decibel noise output, scent emission radius, and minimum required foot traffic. The logic must evaluate these seven physical and environmental constraints for the food court, electronics wing, apparel corridor, and outdoor plaza separately because each zone has different maximum allowances and compatibility rules. It returns the best matching zone for each vendor. Example input: a coffee kiosk needing ten feet width, fifteen amps, and high water supply. Output: the food court zone.

title: Cheerleading Pyramid Structural Assessor
spec: Determines if a gymnastic stunt group is safe by calculating the load distribution when calling `evaluate(formations)`. The system must process the base layer, middle layer, and flyer positions by factoring in the body weight, standing height, static balance score, dynamic strength score, flexibility metric, and years of experience for each athlete. Each of the three structural layers requires a specific safety calculation formula that takes all six of these athlete factors to output a stability rating. Example input: a heavy base combined with a highly flexible, light flyer. Output: a safe formation status.

title: Tubular Wind Chime Tuner
spec: Calculates the resonant frequencies and strike force for a set of outdoor chimes with `simulate(chimes)`. For each tube, the logic must analyze the material density, metal wall thickness, outer cylinder diameter, overall length, suspension hole distance, striker disc mass, and wind catcher sail area. It must classify the chime into soprano, alto, tenor, or bass by passing these seven physical parameters into specific acoustic frequency band formulas. Example input: a thin, long aluminum tube with a large sail. Output: a tenor classification with a soft strike force requirement.

title: Party Pinata Fracture Modeler
spec: Predicts how many strikes a papier mache figure will withstand using `assess(pinatas)`. The calculation relies on the number of paper layers, the flour to water glue ratio, the internal hollow volume, the total candy weight, the suspension rope tension, the average bat swing velocity, and the impact angle. The logic needs to evaluate standard, reinforced, and giant party figures using different mechanical stress formulas for each shape type that require all seven variables. Example input: a heavy candy load with thin paper layers and high swing velocity. Output: a low strike survival count.

title: Airport Carousel Luggage Distributer
spec: Sorts incoming flight baggage to the correct pickup belts via `route(bags)`. The decision depends on the bag weight, horizontal length, vertical height, casing rigidity, passenger priority status, connecting flight time tightness, and declared fragility. Bags must be routed to the oversized belt, the fragile handoff area, the priority express carousel, or the standard main carousel by passing all seven criteria into dedicated routing rule functions for each area. Example input: a large, heavy, non rigid bag with standard priority. Output: the oversized baggage belt assignment.

title: Jigsaw Puzzle Die Cutter Planner
spec: Configures the mechanical press that slices cardboard into interlocking pieces when running `plan(puzzles)`. The setup requires the total piece count, horizontal aspect ratio, vertical cardboard thickness, printed image complexity, interlocking knob depth, connecting tab width, and edge blank margin. The system determines the optimal blade pressure, press speed, and sorting bin size for children, standard, and expert difficulty puzzles by evaluating the seven dimensions through specific manufacturing formulas. Example input: a thousand piece thick cardboard puzzle with high image complexity. Output: high blade pressure and slow press speed.

title: Marionette Rigging Articulation
spec: Computes the balance and control string layout for a wooden puppet by calling `articulate(puppets)`. It evaluates the carved head mass, solid torso mass, wooden arm length, wooden leg length, total string count, wooden control bar width, and joint pivot friction. The system must generate specific rigging coordinates for human, animal, and mythological puppet frames by passing all seven physical properties into distinct gravitational balance equations. Example input: a heavy torso with long limbs and low joint friction. Output: a wide control bar requirement with high string tension.

title: Topiary Garden Shrub Sculpting
spec: Plans the clipping schedule to form geometric shapes from living bushes using `sculpt(shrubs)`. The planner uses the botanical species growth rate, current plant height, woody branch density, average leaf size, desired final geometric shape, daily sunlight exposure, and soil moisture level. The system calculates pruning dates and cut depths for spherical, cubic, and spiral topiary designs by routing these seven growth factors into shape specific maintenance calculators. Example input: a fast growing, dense shrub shaped into a sphere in high sunlight. Output: a weekly pruning schedule.

title: Murder Mystery Dinner Plotter
spec: Validates the consistency of a fictional crime scenario by executing `plot(mysteries)`. Each character must be analyzed using their primary motive score, alibi believability strength, murder weapon access level, interpersonal relationship tension, secret hidden wealth, timeline gap duration, and hidden alternate identity. The logic validates the victim, the prime suspect, the red herring, and the actual culprit by passing all seven narrative constraints into separate consistency checks for each role. Example input: a suspect with high weapon access, a long timeline gap, and high secret wealth. Output: successfully flagged as the culprit.

title: Footwear Lacing Friction Assessor
spec: Determines the tightness and slide resistance of different shoe tying patterns with `lace(shoes)`. The calculation requires the total eyelet count, vertical spacing between holes, horizontal spacing across the tongue, fabric lace material friction, lace cord thickness, tongue padding thickness, and wearer instep curve. The system must score the crisscross, straight bar, and heel lock lacing methods by applying the seven variables to tension formulas for each pattern type. Example input: thick cotton laces with close vertical spacing and a high instep. Output: a high slide resistance score.

title: Incense Stick Formulation
spec: Calculates the burning characteristics of aromatic sticks when running `blend(incense)`. The logic processes the binding resin ratio, the wood powder mesh size, the essential oil concentration percentage, the target burn time, the desired smoke volume, the drying room curing humidity, and the dye colorant amount. Formulations are categorized into meditation, outdoor, and ceremonial grades, requiring dedicated mixing functions that ingest all seven properties to output a quality score. Example input: high oil concentration with fine wood powder and low resin. Output: a ceremonial grade stick with low smoke output.

title: Hamster Maze Architect
spec: Evaluates the safety and difficulty of a rodent obstacle course via `design(mazes)`. The assessment needs the plastic corridor length, tunnel width, upward incline angle, side wall height, floor texture grip coefficient, food treat frequency, and spinning wheel diameter. The design must be scored for dwarf, syrian, and roborovski breeds by testing the seven dimensions against the physical limits and agility formulas of each specific breed. Example input: a steep incline with low floor grip and sparse treats. Output: an unsafe rating for a dwarf breed.

title: Winter Snow Sculpture Modeler
spec: Assesses the structural integrity of carved ice and snow displays by calling `model(sculptures)`. It calculates collapse risk using the ambient air temperature, snow water content percentage, mechanical compaction density, foundation base width, unsupported top width, cantilever overhang angle, and directional wind load profile. The model checks the stability of castle, animal, and abstract shapes by routing these seven climatic and geometric factors into specific architectural load formulas. Example input: high water content snow with a large overhang angle and high wind. Output: a severe collapse risk warning.

title: Box Kite Stability Rater
spec: Determines the optimal flying weather for geometric kites using `evaluate(kites)`. The rating depends on the hollow cell count, wooden spar length, wooden spar flexibility, nylon fabric porosity, tow bridle attachment point, fabric tail length, and minimum wind speed rating. The logic must process standard box, winged box, and star box designs, creating a distinct flight profile for each by combining the seven aerodynamic properties in specialized lift formulas. Example input: a high cell count kite with low fabric porosity and rigid spars. Output: a stable flight profile suitable for strong winds.

title: Mosaic Tile Mural Generator
spec: Calculates the layout and material requirements for large wall art via `arrange(murals)`. The generator needs the individual tile side length, ceramic thickness, glass opacity level, primary color hue, color saturation intensity, cement grout width, and thermal expansion coefficient. It computes the total cost and structural weight for indoor, outdoor, and submerged pool murals by passing these seven attributes into environment specific calculator functions. Example input: high thermal expansion tiles placed in an outdoor setting with thin grout. Output: a structural warning for thermal cracking risk.

title: Bank Vault Security Array
spec: Configures the alarm thresholds for a secure storage facility by executing `distribute(vaults)`. The configuration requires the steel door thickness, floor seismic sensor count, ceiling thermal sensor count, invisible laser grid density, time lock maximum duration, concrete wall reinforcement rating, and video camera coverage percentage. The system must establish daytime, nighttime, and lockdown security states, applying all seven variables to the specific sensitivity threshold formulas for each operational state. Example input: a nighttime state with low camera coverage and high wall reinforcement. Output: increased sensitivity required for seismic and thermal sensors.

title: Meteorological Weather Balloon Rigger
spec: Determines the ascent profile for an atmospheric data probe when running `pack(payloads)`. The calculation involves the rubber latex thickness, expanding helium volume, total payload weight, radio telemetry rate, digital camera resolution, descent parachute area, and radar reflector size. The logic simulates the flight path through the troposphere, stratosphere, and mesosphere, requiring all seven parameters to calculate the estimated burst altitude and descent speed for each atmospheric layer. Example input: a large helium volume with thin latex and a heavy payload. Output: a low altitude burst event followed by a fast descent.
